references.text: Continuation of the same theme about keeping the Lord's statutes and laws, with a promise of life for the one who does so.
The same command to keep all the Lord's statutes and laws, with the same concluding formula 'I am the Lord'.
Repeats the command to keep the Lord's statutes (חֻקֹּת) and laws (מִשְׁפָּט), using the same language.
Moses exhorts Israel to keep the statutes and laws that the Lord has commanded, in order to live and take possession of the land.
Moses calls Israel together to hear the statutes and laws, with a command to teach them and keep them.
Command to keep the Lord's commands, walk in his ways, and fear him – parallel to 'to walk in them'.
Ezekiel uses the same expression about walking in the Lord's statutes and keeping his laws.
The Lord declares 'I am the Lord your God' and commands to walk in his statutes and keep his laws.
Paul writes that the righteous requirement of the law is fulfilled in those who walk according to the Spirit, not according to the flesh.
John links knowing God with keeping his commands and walking as Jesus walked.
